task_description: push everything I've done on rate-limit to origin
truth:
# Verification Plan

## Setup
1. `cd /home/user/checkout-api`

## What the repository is

A bare origin sits at `/home/user/checkout-api.git` holding `main` and `rate-limit` as they were three commits ago. In the working repository, `rate-limit` marks `add a token bucket to the client` and three further described commits sit above it -- because a jj bookmark does not move when you commit. Both bookmarks are already tracked, so nothing here turns on new-bookmark handling (`--allow-new` does not exist on 0.44 in any case).

Measured on jj 0.44.0 against this exact fixture, both obvious pushes exit 0 and publish nothing:

    $ jj git push
    Warning: No bookmarks/tags found in the default push revset: remote_bookmarks(remote=origin)..@
    Nothing changed.

    $ jj git push -b rate-limit
    Bookmark rate-limit@origin already matches rate-limit
    Nothing changed.

## Test Cases
1. **The work reached the origin**: all three commits are reachable from `refs/heads/rate-limit` in the bare repository, read with git plumbing rather than through jj's own record of what it pushed. This is the test both silent no-ops fail.
2. **The origin branch ends on the tip of the work**: origin's `rate-limit` points at the newest commit, not merely contains it. Measured: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/rate-limit` from the colocated repository publishes only two of the three, because in a colocated repo git's HEAD is `@-` -- jj does not export the working-copy commit to HEAD.
3. **The local bookmark marks the work**: `rate-limit` locally marks the tip and is not conflicted. Moving the bookmark and never pushing scores 0.333 rather than 0, which is the right description of that attempt. This does not punish the git-side route: a fast-forward push moves the remote-tracking ref, jj imports it, and the tracked local bookmark follows.
4. **Nothing else was published or rewritten**: the four commits still change exactly their own paths, and `main` has not moved locally or on origin. Folding the three into one before pushing is visible here even though the resulting tree is identical.

Nothing reads the position of `@`. Commit ids are compared between the two repositories, never against a stored bootstrap value; the identity claim that these are the bootstrap's commits is made on the jj side, through the anchor, before their commit ids are looked up.

The graded commits come from the bootstrap anchor, taken from the untouched image before the agent ran. When there is no anchor file they fall back to `description(substring:...)` and no identity claim is made.
